text:
New Jersey made it three straight wins on Saturday night, and the way they got there says more than the 3-1 score. The Devils had to wait through a scoreless first period and then a one-goal deficit before the pressure they'd been applying finally paid off. Scott Laughton gave Los Angeles the lead late in the second period on a wrist shot our numbers rated at an 11 percent chance. Anthony Mantha answered 2:46 later, and Brett Pesce put New Jersey ahead early in the third. Arseny Gritsyuk added an insurance goal with 65 seconds left.

The play was lopsided. New Jersey out-attempted Los Angeles 61 to 37, and on expected goals (a measure of chance quality) the Devils led 3.34 to 1.38. Our simulations say the Devils deserved to win 82 percent of the time, meaning that share of replays of every shot ended in their favor. The second period was the clearest stretch: 1.69 expected goals to 0.44. The Kings' goal came during that stretch, on one of their few good looks.

Anton Forsberg kept Los Angeles in it. He faced shots worth 3.24 expected goals and allowed two, saving about 1.2 goals more than an average goalie would have. Luke Evangelista had the best chance that didn't go in, a 22 percent look in the second that Forsberg stopped. Pesce, who the Hurricanes drafted 66th overall out of New Hampshire in 2013, logged 21:30 and scored the go-ahead goal. The win stretches New Jersey's streak to three. For Los Angeles, the loss is a game they were lucky to keep that close.
